doc.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998

title: Norvo's subtle 1940 band and the dance circuit
summary: George Simon's quote about the 1940 Norvo band and the one-nighters, hotels and college dates.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Yeah. There’s actually a little quote from this book Inside the Big Bands by a fellow Simon—

He says, “Red came back with another ten piece band in the spring of 1940. This one featured two brilliant young trumpeters, Conrad Gozzo and Rusty Dedrick.” He then says, “It produced the same sort of a soft, subtle swing that his 1936 group had,” and he went on to say that, “it may have been a little too subtle for what was going on.”
It was, yeah, right. It didn’t hit you over the head at all. That’s why he was never able to get into the big money. But musically it was great.

Yes, some concerts, but mostly one nighters, college dates and hotels. Like there used to be — I don’t know if they exist today — but the Ben Franklin Hotel in Philadelphia, Huehlbach Hotel in Kansas City. Red and I was talking about that the other day. The hotel had pillars with all mirrors. We were laughing about that.
